observations: Three close-up photos of a large diesel inline engine, likely 6-cylinder, shown from different angles.
Engine surfaces show heavy rust, flaking red and grey paint, and dirt/oil grime consistent with age and outdoor storage.
Visible pulleys, belts, injector lines, fuel rail, and what appears to be a turbo housing on the right side in photo 0.
Background in all three photos shows other stripped engines and parts, indicating a scrapyard or used-parts dealer setting.
A 'POSTED ON JIJI / CHARLES UMEH' watermark appears across all photos; no manufacturer nameplate, data plate, or serial number is visible or legible in any shot.
No photo shows the engine running, connected to electrics, or undergoing any test (compression, start-up, smoke).

claims.claim: This is an Iveco Eurocargo engine, powered by Tector 5 or Tector 7 diesel engines
claims.evidence: No nameplate, casting mark, or engine code is visible or legible in photo 0, 1, or 2; claim rests solely on seller's text.
No start-up, running, or compression test shown in any photo; surface rust visible in photo 0 and photo 1 raises doubt but does not confirm internal condition either way.

risks.risk: Engine may not start or run (internal wear, seized components, corrosion from sitting outside)
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine being started and idling, with audible sound and visible smoke/exhaust

risks.risk: Engine identity (make/model) cannot be confirmed, which affects compatibility and value
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine data plate, block casting number, or ECU/injection pump tag
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic used diesel truck engine of unconfirmed origin, not as a named Iveco Tector unit

risks.risk: Completeness unknown — turbo, injection pump, alternator, starter, manifolds may be missing or swapped
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photo set including front (timing cover), rear (flywheel housing), and underside (oil pan/sump)
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming missing ancillary parts not clearly visible

risks.risk: Visible rust and paint flaking could indicate long-term outdoor storage, raising risk of corrosion in cylinders, injectors, or fuel system
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cylinder bores (via removed head or inspection port) and fuel system components

proof_requests: Video of the engine running/idling with sound
Clear photo of engine data/serial plate or block casting number
Photos of front timing cover, rear flywheel housing, and underside/oil pan
Photo showing fuel injection pump and turbo tag/markings close up
response.reason: The photos show a genuine used diesel engine but carry no readable brand or model marking, and no evidence of it running; it must be priced as an unverified, unidentified used diesel truck engine at worst-case (non-running, completeness unconfirmed) condition.
